about: Insights from 'The Standardized Soil Moisture-Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI): daily scale global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes (1961-2023)', Earth System Science Data 18, 7981-8002, 2026 (published 3 November 2026, CC BY 4.0), DOI 10.5194/essd-18-7981-2026, supplied by the owner as a PDF. A daily, global estimate from reanalysis (ERA5-Land soil moisture and ERA5 maximum temperature), not station measurements; it reports no country-level result for South or Southeast Asia, and its one Asian hotspot is China's Yangtze River Basin. stage.js writes data/inbox/2026-11-compound-dry-hot/sources.json; verify-sources.yml checks each term on the publisher's open PDF; apply.js uses only confirmed claims. What was held back is in ledger.md.

sources.title: The Standardized Soil Moisture-Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI): daily scale global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes (1961-2023)

claims.text: In hotspot regions, compound dry-hot events have become more frequent in the recent warming period (2000-2023) than in 1961-1999, and their joint occurrence rises faster than the two drivers alone would imply.
rests_on: joint occurrence rises faster than the independent combination

claims.text: In China's Yangtze River Basin, the median event count per grid cell rose from 10 in 1961-1999 to 21 in 2000-2023.
The data set is built from reanalysis and does not represent irrigation.
